title: CmdPal: Extension SDK 0.12.260812002 can't be used with project using old .NET versions

actions.label: Approve CmdPal SDK compatibility design
actions.note: Approve a design that lowers or multi-targets the public Command Palette extension SDK instead of inheriting the repo-wide net10 floor.

actions.label: Reproduce older-TFM SDK incompatibility
actions.note: Give a maintainer a concrete compatibility repro before locking the supported target-framework matrix.

reproduce.version_requirement: Use the current 0.12.x Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions package line against an older .NET Windows TFM project.
prerequisites: A clean sample extension project that targets a lower Windows .NET TFM (for example a current supported net8/net9 Windows target) instead of net10.
The public Command Palette extension SDK package reference.
steps: Create or edit a sample Command Palette extension project so it targets the intended lower supported Windows TFM instead of net10.
Add the current Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions SDK package/reference and restore dependencies.
Build the project and capture whether NuGet/MSBuild requires a retarget to net10 or fails because the toolkit/template assets only expose net10-compatible targets.
After implementing the compatibility fix, repeat the same restore/build on the lower TFM and on the current net10 template path.
reproduce.expected_result: The public extension SDK should restore and build on the chosen supported lower TFM without forcing extension authors to retarget their whole project to net10.

issue_context.summary: The public Command Palette extension SDK and its template currently assume net10, preventing extension projects that stay on older .NET Windows targets from consuming the package cleanly.
known_information: The repo-wide .NET props currently set net10 as the common target floor.
The Toolkit csproj imports those common props and does not override the inherited target framework.
The extension template csproj independently hard-codes net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0.
The issue was filed by jiripolasek, who also owns other recent CmdPal technical work in this batch.
inferences: The public package was upgraded in lockstep with the PowerToys app repo, but extension consumers do not necessarily share the same TFM floor as the PowerToys app itself.
The design probably needs an SDK-specific target-floor property and a compatibility build check so future repo-wide framework upgrades do not regress the package again.
issue_context.analysis: This is actionable design work even without a full implementation-grade expansion in this batch. The source pinpoints the packaging problem, and the remaining question is the exact compatibility policy the maintainer wants to support.
initial_investigation: Reviewed src/Common.Dotnet.props for the repo-wide target floor.
Reviewed the public Toolkit csproj and confirmed it inherits the common props.
Reviewed the template csproj and confirmed it hard-codes net10.

judgment.rationale: Current Command Palette extension SDK packaging still inherits or hard-codes a net10 Windows target, which blocks extension projects that intentionally remain on older supported .NET TFMs.
evidence: src/modules/cmdpal/extensionsdk/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit.csproj imports the common props and does not override TargetFramework.
The issue was filed by the Command Palette owner after clearing the generic Needs-Author-Feedback label, so it reflects a real SDK packaging concern rather than a vague external report.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a packaging design that decouples the public extension SDK and template from the repo-wide net10 floor, and verify the supported lower-TFM story with a concrete reproduction project.

fix_assessment.rationale: A public SDK packaging fix is appropriate, but the lowest supported TFM and multi-targeting shape still need maintainer confirmation.

proposed_fixes.title: Decouple the public CmdPal extension SDK from the repo-wide net10 target floor
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The public Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit package inherits the repository’s `CoreTargetFramework=net10.0`, and the extension template hard-codes net10 as well, so consuming extension projects targeting older .NET Windows TFMs cannot use the SDK without retargeting.
plan: Introduce an SDK-specific target-framework property or TargetFrameworks list for the public extension package instead of inheriting the repo-wide app TFM unchanged.
Update the template project to use the same supported SDK TFM floor rather than hard-coding net10.
Add a validation project or build check that restores and builds a sample extension on the lowest supported TFM so future repo-wide upgrades do not silently break SDK consumers.
verification: Create a sample extension project targeting the chosen lower supported TFM, add Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions 0.12.x, and confirm restore/build succeed without retargeting to net10.
Build the existing template and current net10 consumer path to ensure the broader SDK compatibility change does not regress the newest supported configuration.

confidence.rationale: The packaging problem is obvious in source, but the exact supported lower TFM and whether the package should multi-target or simply lower its floor still need maintainer choice.
